October 2009 ## Growth in Asian output y-o-y but not elsewhere yet - The biggest story has to be the anti-dumping petition signed by Cerro Flow, KobeWieland and Mueller against Chinese and Mexican seamless copper tube fabricators. From an independent point of view, the exporters have indeed seized some market share in the US copper tube industry by selling at a much lower price. However, one can also argue that this has been the result of a long term business strategy and the benefit from offshoring production to lower cost locations. - The market is split into three very different stories. Asia continued to see signs of improvement in all segments, with South Korea reporting a drastic upturn in alloy rod output in August and China showing a consistent recovery in total domestic consumption. Demand remains sluggish in North America in Q3, particularly weak in the copper flat rolled product and brass rod markets. Mixed signals are seen from the European markets. 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 12 **October 2009** Copper and copper alloy mill products www.crumonitor.com # Plate, sheet, strip and foil ### Japanese flat rolled product output is recovering **Nippon Mining & Metals** is planning to raise its rolled copper output to 3,100t per month in H2 FY2009, reaching the peak levels achieved in H1 FY2008. This is supported by recovered demand for personal computers and flat TV panels. Currently, the company estimates that demand has improved by 70-90% compared to its peak in H1 FY2008. Other plans of Nippon include the expansion of its original copper foil (HS1200) sales. This is used in automotive lithium ion batteries, featuring thinness and higher strength compared to electrolytic copper foil. Also, it offers improved heat resistance compared to conventional rolled copper foil; scratches and wrinkles on the surface can be decreased. Even though HS1200 contains tin, it has 90% electric conductivity. Considering the growing market for electric and hybrid vehicles, this product series has great market potential. In the meantime, **Hitachi Cable** will increase its rolled copper production by 16% in H2 FY2009 compared to H1 FY2009. In addition, **Dowa Metaltech** is restoring production of copper plate and strip; the company is planning to increase its workforce by 30 by the end of FY2009. Full-scale operations at its two production subsidiaries are to start in October. Copper strip production will rise to satisfy growing demand from the semiconductor industry. According to the **Japan Copper & Brass Association** , brass strip output contracted in August by 15% y-o-y, which is a much smaller reduction compared to other copper and alloy semis segments. ### China: strong demand from the IT and automotive sectors CRU’s market contacts reported that demand for flat rolled products from the electronics and automotive industries outperformed other sectors. In particular, high-precision copper plate, sheet and strip exhibited strong performance supported by demand from the computer and electronic industries. Demand for normal precision copper alloy plate, sheet and strip remained flat. In the alloy foil segment, market participants said that demand was stable while competition in medium-grade products was intense. Market conditions and demand in the high-grade products segment were better. ### Europe is concerned about sustainability issue

s 

**Swissmetal** announced that it will focus again on its core business.  The company intends to reinforce its technical sales support team by increasing the number of personnel whilst its European and Asian operations will focus on sales and marketing of the Swissmetal brand.  However, with a view to reducing costs, Swissmetal will dissolve its **Avins** subsidiaries in Germany and Switzerland.  The Hong-Kong based Avins company will be renamed **Swissmetal East Asia** .  In H1 2009, Swissmetal suffered a 43% y-o-y plunge in gross sales to CHF103 million (US$102 million).  But the company is seeing that the market environment will improve in the months to come and is ready to participate in the market growth. In H1 2009, rolled products represented 19% of **Halcor’s** sales volume.  The company reported that as a result of the slowdown in construction activity, its rolling products for roofing were impacted. **KME** said that further to the significant contraction its roofing products experienced in 2008, the situation in H1 2009 was more stable with recovered volumes in Italy, Germany, Benelux, Russia and Ukraine.  The company has benefited from downstream expansion to architectural applications of copper.  Market contacts reported that although demand was better in Q3 compared to Q1 and Q2, it was far behind the average of 2008.  However, as stock levels in the supply chain are so low, any upturn in business activity has and will have an immediate effect on demand.  Northern Europe, especially Germany, is in a better position compared to Southern Europe.  Supported by government incentives, the automotive industry is now performing well, but its future growth remains to be seen.  Market recovery is expected to be slow and unlikely to be smooth.  The main concern is the sustainability of the current positive momentum given that most market participants, primarily the small ones, are suffering from poor visibility.

We think that the other market participants in the US copper tube industry will have different views on the case.  Producers such as **Luvata** and **IUSA** , who have already built mills in Mexico, may probably not support the petition. 

### Europe still feels the downturn despite some optimism 

Even thought there is evident optimism for 2010, market participants do not give positive feedback yet. According to **Assomet** , Italian demand for copper and alloy semis in 2010 is projected to add up to 936,600t from an estimated 894,200 in 2009.  Production in 2010 is expected to be 968,300t compared to an estimated 923,600t this year.  When **KME** published its H1 2009 sales figures, it reported that consolidated revenues plummeted by 44.6% y-o-y.  In particular, the ongoing crisis in the construction sector impacted tube sales for water heating systems.  Shipments to the UK, Spain and Eastern Europe were significantly affected.  Industrial tubes did not perform well either, as weak demand in the air con sector was not fully offset by good performance in the renewable energy and fittings sectors. In Greece, **Halcor’s** consolidated turnover in H1 2009 registered a 51% y-o-y fall; volumes dropped by 33% y-o-y. The copper tube business accounts for 27% of its total sales volume.  Halcor attributed the sales decline to the slowdown in construction activity and the fall in demand for copper industrial products.  Europe was also impacted by the overall mood of uncertainty that led to production cuts and tighter inventory management.  CRU’s contacts expressed their concern about rising copper prices and price volatility that have once again triggered copper substitution issues, especially in the vulnerable tube segment. 

### Tube innovation and strong competition in Japan 

The Japanese copper tube industry is leading the way in copper tube innovation through research in alloy tube fabrication, primarily for air cons and refrigerators. **Sumitomo Light Metal Industries** is to start production of high-strength copper alloy tubes; the patent is owned by **Mitsubishi Materials** .  Also, **Kobelco & Materials Copper Tube** will double its high-strength alloy tube output to 400t per month by FY2011.  However, due to increased competition, the company intends to reduce its total costs by 10% so as to return to profitability by FY2010; this will include a 20% cut in its workforce. **Hitachi Cable** , facing delayed recovery in the tube segment, is expecting lower demand for its copper tube products in H2 of FY2009.  From a recovery perspective, the overall picture in Japan is currently mixed. 

### China: the big factor 

**China Nonferrous Metal Mining** acquired a controlling stake in **Shandong Albetter Albronze** , a copper tube and flat rolled products fabricator.  The acquisition will help Albetter expand in the future. Albetter’s annual copper tube capacity

Volumes declined 21.8% y-o-y for the first three quarters. The global picture among industrialised countries is reasonably consistent. In Western Europe and North America, output has fallen by around a third, with North East Asia faring only a little better with a contraction of just over a quarter. China is the only major country to show growth in the first three quarters, a modest 3.4% y-o-y. Fourth quarter volumes will look more positive year-on-year due to the weakness of Q4 last year, but we expect little sequential improvement on Q3. Recovery in 2010 is likely to be slow and limited, with volumes regaining only a little ground against 2008. Market visibility remains poor, and end-users are taking a cautious approach. Although recent economic indicators offer signs of optimism, it remains to be seen if the current stimulus-fuelled recovery can be sustained. Fabricators report that generally larger accounts are in a better position than small and medium sized customers, who are continuing to suffer the most from obtaining and guaranteeing credit. ### US volume increases slightly US alloy rod output showed a slight sequential recovery to 47,800t in Q3. For the first three quarters production was down 38.1% y-o-y. Automotive has seen some improvement recently following government incentives. However, construction demand remains very weak with little prospect of significant improvement in 2010 as the commercial sector slows. **Mueller Industries** , in its recently released Q3 financial results, posted improved earnings for its OEM segment of $16.5M versus $10.6M in 2008. This was despite a decline in sales volume to $181.6M from $299.5M as a result of lower raw material costs, and volumes that were reported to be substantially lo

wer for most core product lines. ### Germany is Europe’s best performer Northern Europe, particularly Germany, is currently seeing better demand that Southern Europe. Spain and Italy are still experiencing difficulty. The automotive sector is seeing the most improved demand but with much of this strength deriving from scrapping schemes and other government incentives, there remains a question mark over future demand. Italy’s **KME Group** expects to see a recovery of about 1015% y-o-y in 2010. KME's output in the second half of this year should improve on the first half when it dropped 30% y-o-y to 218,000t, but full-year production will still be heavily down on 2008. Among product initiatives this year, **Wieland** and **Diehl Metall** are jointly marketing a lead-free brass under the brand-name ‘Cuphin’. Previously, a lead-free copper alloy was offered by Wieland under the brand name ‘Ecobrass’ and by Diehl under the brand name ‘Diehl 430 PbF’. The product is being marketed in anticipation of future regulatory requirements, including an EU directive which requires the lead content of drinking water to be reduced from a maximum of 25μg/l to 10μg/l by 2013. ### Asian countries show y-o-y growth in Q3 Chinese demand for alloy rod and wire increased in Q2 compared with Q1. Consumption remained stable in Q3. Leading fabricator **Ningbo Jintian** has experienced its copper alloy bar output fall short of demand recently, and it is producing at nearly full capacity. The company estimates demand will remain flat q-oq in Q4. Taiwan is showing the most positive prospects in North East Asia, with our current forecast being that Q3 volumes are set to be up 18.4% on the previous quarter and up 10.4% y-o-y, as the country benefits from China’s strength. In South Korea, Q3 output is also showing gains, up 11.9% y-o-y. August copper and alloy bar output was up 7.1% y-o-y to 18,906t. tinued to act at odds with fundamentals, breaking through the $6,000/t barrier despite rising exchange stocks and still weak copper demand.  The market continues to react to favourable interpretations of macro economic news.  Ongoing weakness of the US dollar has also given support to prices.   After breaking through $6,000/t in August, three-month prices continued to climb to reach a high of $6,540/t by the end of the month.  By late September, prices had slipped towards $5,850/t, suggesting that the market was reacting to the slow and steady increase in inventories.  However, prices soon returned above $6,000/t and have continued to climb in October, the official price reaching $6,444/t on 20<sup>th</sup> October.  We anticipate that prices will continue to be investor driven for the remainder of 2009, remaining vulnerable to a change of sentiment. 

#### **Zinc** 

Zinc prices have continued to recover.  The cash price broke through $2,000/t on 9<sup>th</sup> October for the first time since July 2008.  LME stock levels have fallen more than 10,000t since tipping 438,050t on 1<sup>st</sup> September, after building more than 100,000t since May.  Zinc demand has improved since the start of the year, but supply is also recovering, with Nyrstar recently reinstating output, and the market remains in surplus.

The company employs 270 at the plant whilst the job cuts amount to 12% of the workforce. For the nine months to September, net sales of Mueller Industries plunged by 48% y-oy. Q3 net sales were down by 37% y-o-y. It is anticipated that the market conditions in the residential and commercial building sectors will continue to challenge the company in 2010. - According to data released by **the Copper and Brass Fabricators Council,** US imports of brass mill products in August contracted by 40% y-o-y and exports by 23% y-o-y. August imports of all brass mill products amounted to 33,722,170lbs while exports totalled 16,794,773lbs. In the flat rolled product segment, imports were 7,518,345lbs and exports 5,916,108lbs. Tube and pipe imports reached 18,186,279lbs whilst exports 5,446,636lbs. Finally, exports of rods, bars and sections totalled 3,538,226lbs; imports added up to 6,130,905lbs. - **The Internation

al Copper Association** is promoting a new process for brazing copper and brass. This involves multiport tube assemblies made of two matching CuproBraze alloy strips, and the design of products for brazing different types of joints simultaneously.  Heat exchangers are to benefit from this and CuproBraze technology can have an important role in this development. 

### Europe 









- **KME,** the Italian copper and alloy semis manufacturer, said that it anticipates market demand to recover in Q4 2009.  KME sees that the market in 2009 will contract by 25% y-o-y; in H1 2009, sales plummeted by 30% y-o-y.  The company expects that total output of its copper and alloy products will add up to 450,000t in 2009.  In addition, KME reported that its consumption of copper cathodes and ingots in 2008 reached 600,000t. 

- **Swissmetal,** the Swiss copper semis fabricator, is expecting that its demand for copper in 2009 may plunge by 20-30% y-o-y.  But considering the current recovery signs, the company remains optimistic for 2010.  More customer enquiries and business activity are currently being experienced compared to the beginning of 2009.  In response to the slowdown, Swissmetal decreased its in-house stock levels, keeping a three-month stock policy.  The plan is to keep operating at these efficient levels with reduced complexity and production time (e.g. small number of different billet diameters). 

- **Luvata** reported that it will reactivate idled capacity in Europe and the US in 2010.  This is attributed to the recovery that the company sees on a month-on-month basis.  The Chinese plants that produce tubes for air conditioners resumed production in the second half of June after a monthlong cut.  Luvata anticipates that its growth will be a function of GDP as well as market share gains. 

- **Feinrohren,** the Italian copper tube maker, announced that it will start up a new plant focusing on the production of thin wall copper tube for the ACR market.  With this new project, the company will raise its copper tube capacity from 50,000t to 90,000t per annum. 

### North East Asia 





- **The Japan Copper and Brass Association** said that output of flat rolled products in Japan increased by 2.2% m-o-m in August.  The figure provides some optimism that demand for copper semi-finished products is exhibiting signs of recovery; this is more evident in the automobile and semiconductor sectors.  But from a y-o-y perspective, the seasonally adjusted production figure of August is down by 21% to 63,224t.  Industry officials see that copper consumption in Japan has returned to 70-80% of 2008 levels. 

- Japanese copper and alloy semis shipments are anticipated to total 713,930t in FY2009.  This represents an 11.5% y-o-y decline, said the Japan Copper and Brass Association.  Deliveries of brass bars are projected to decline by 18.4% to 154,090t, mainly due to the troubled construction sector. Copper tube sales are expected to fall by 13.7% to 121,950t.  It

is reported that 80% of copper tubes are supplied to air con and refrigerator makers, which are still seeing low demand.  Copper sheet and strip offtake is anticipated to decline by 3.8% to 221,270t.  In July-August, demand for copper sheet

### Developing Asia 





- Data released by the Beijing-based customs office showed that Chinese imports of refined copper and copper semi-finished products added up to 399,052t in September.  This is a 23% m-o-m increase.  As market analysts widely anticipated another m-o-m fall in September, the figure exceeded expectations.  A reason why analysts expected a fall was due to the current price differential that does not favour Chinese imports of copper. 

- **Ningbo Jintian Copper Tube** , a Chinese copper tube maker, said that demand for its products is low.  The company commented that the majority of its customers are located outside of China and have not realised a pick up in demand yet.
